detail.longDescription: I've been assigned this problem/exercise to solve at uni: Write a program in python which gets the date of Easter Orthodox Sunday during a specific year. I've been given an algorithm to follow and I've written the function: ortho_easter(year) , which basically does the job (no issues there) and returns a tuple of the form: (day, month, year) Now, as a follow up question: during the 21st century, what is the date that Easter Orthodox Sunday falls the earliest in the year? This obviously calls for a for loop. for year in range(2000,2101): dates_list=[] dates_list.append(ortho_easter(year)) Additionally, Easter Orthodox Sunday either falls on April or May, so I can take for granted that month == 4 . How can I check from the tuples for which month == 4 holds true, which has the lowest "day" value, and following that, get the respective tuple so I can print it?
